# The software reference is the library's own portable SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256, compiled here for
# the board's CPU exactly as an ESP build of iclforge::base would take them: sha256.cpp and
# hmac_sha256.cpp with the hw/none/ member of the SHA-256 hardware seam (libs/base/CMakeLists.txt
# picks that directory when there is no kernel for the architecture).
get_filename_component(ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../../libs/base" ABSOLUTE)

# The library's export header is generated by its own CMake, which this project does not run, so the
# two sources are built against a stand-in written into this build's directory: nothing is exported or
# imported. It is not a file of the tree because the layering check reads every
# iclforge/base/export.hpp as the library's. ESP-IDF runs this file once to read the requirements,
# without a build directory to write to.
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_EARLY_EXPANSION)
    file(WRITE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/shim/iclforge/base/export.hpp"
        "#pragma once\n#define ICLFORGE_BASE_EXPORT\n")
endif()

# The crypto clock selector exists on the ESP32-P4 only (crypto_clock.hpp): a file for the chip that
# has it and one for the others, chosen here, never an #if in the source.
if(IDF_TARGET STREQUAL "esp32p4")
    set(ICLFORGE_BENCH_CLOCK crypto_clock_esp32p4.cpp)
else()
    set(ICLFORGE_BENCH_CLOCK crypto_clock_none.cpp)
endif()

# How the bench hands its pass back (net_report.hpp): the console only, or over the P4X kit's Ethernet
# port for a board that has no USB. -DCRYPTO_BENCH_REPORT=ethernet on the idf.py command line.
if(CRYPTO_BENCH_REPORT STREQUAL "ethernet")
    set(ICLFORGE_BENCH_REPORT net_report_ethernet.cpp)
else()
    set(ICLFORGE_BENCH_REPORT net_report_none.cpp)
endif()

idf_component_register(
    SRCS
        crypto_bench.cpp
        "${ICLFORGE_BENCH_CLOCK}"
        "${ICLFORGE_BENCH_REPORT}"
        "${ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR}/src/crypto/sha256.cpp"
        "${ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR}/src/crypto/hmac_sha256.cpp"
        "${ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR}/src/crypto/hw/none/sha256_hw.cpp"
    PRIV_INCLUDE_DIRS
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/shim"
        "${ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR}/include"
        "${ICLFORGE_BASE_DIR}/src"
    # The network components are required by every build, not only the one that uses them: ESP-IDF
    # works out a component's requirements in a CMake script run without the cache, so a -D on the
    # command line (CRYPTO_BENCH_REPORT above) is not there to decide them. An unused one is not linked.
    PRIV_REQUIRES
        mbedtls esp_timer heap freertos esp_hw_support esp_system soc
        esp_eth esp_netif esp_event lwip app_update)
